text:
sana: Heads-up — onboarded v3q4 yesterday. Quick smoke/run showed marginally better overall NDCG but one cohort (applicant_ids) has an elevated hallucination rate. Thinking we should implement a fractional-cohort throttle + hysteresis instead of an immediate rollback. Thoughts?

rohit: can you paste the run summary?

eval-bot: run summary (2026-03-22T15:04Z): comparing v3q4 -> v3 (baseline) over 1h window
```
metric         | overall_delta | cohort:applicant_ids | cohort:payments_card
NDCG           | +0.007        | -0.004               | +0.012
halluc_rate    | -0.0008       | +0.026               | +0.001
delta_p95_ms   | +9ms          | +12ms                | +7ms
requests       | 12,400        | 320                  | 840
```
notes: applicant_ids halluc_rate +0.026 (> hall_thresh 0.02) and samples=320 (>= min_samples 250).

claire: Strong prefer gradual throttle per-cohort with a restore hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping. Also need deterministic sampling so legal can reproduce redacted examples.

sana: Proposed micro-proposal: fractional throttle policy that reduces only matching cohort traffic while leaving global route untouched. Key rules: min_samples=250, hall_thresh=0.02, cohort_throttle = 1 - clamp((hall_delta - hall_thresh) * beta, 0.0, 0.6), restore when hall_delta < hall_thresh * 0.8 for 2 consecutive windows, global_autofallback if weighted_cohort_impact > 0.04 for 20m. Include reproducible seed and S3 path for redacted repros.

rohit: ok but need to define weighted_cohort_impact precisely. I propose: impact = pct_cohort * normalized_hall where normalized_hall = hall_delta / hall_thresh. sum impacts across cohorts.

infra-bot: quick config draft deployed to staging: 
```yaml
policy_name: "sana-fractional-throttle-v1"
window: 10m
min_samples: 250
cohort_metric: "hallucination_rate"
hall_thresh: 0.02
beta: 0.5 # scaling coef for throttle
max_throttle: 0.6 # max reduction fraction
hysteresis: 
  restore_multiplier: 0.8
  restore_windows: 2
global_autofallback:
  impact_threshold: 0.04
  eval_window: 20m
  action: roll_to_baseline
repro: 
  seed: 20260322-01
  redacted_s3: "s3://redwood-evals/repro/4950000001/"
  kms: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:acct:key/abcd-1234"
cooldown: 10m
```

claire: Important: enforce session_affinity when throttling to keep KV-cache warm for users on that cohort. Without it we risk higher tail latency.

rohit: Also suggest we run a synthetic replay on staging with same seed to validate sampling stability. Claire, can you coordinate with infra?

claire: On it. Will schedule a replay job and tag legal for repro samples.

legal: Please ensure applicant_ids repros are redacted for PII and retained only for 90 days. Also ask for an example repro bundle in the PR for review.

sana: Will include redaction rules and retention policy in PR. Also adding a small dashboard: cohort impact gauge, throttle % over time, and rollback counter.

eval-bot: Replay scheduled -> job_id=4950000001-replay-1. Expected artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/repro/4950000001/replay-1 (redacted).

infra-bot: Staging policy applied to /staging/canaries/sana-fractional-throttle-v1. Monitoring output will go to #canary-observability.

rohit: One more note: tune beta so that for hall_delta=0.026 (observed) throttle ~= 0.13 (i.e., small reduction). We want to avoid over-throttling the cohort.

claire: +1. We'll iterate after the replay results.

sana: Thanks — I'll open the PR with the config snippet, reproducible seed, replay links, and a short playbook for oncall to follow if the global_autofallback triggers. :thumbsup:

legal: I'll review the repro bundle once PR is up.

infra-bot: Monitoring: staging alert will fire if any cohort has min_samples>=250 and hall_delta>0.02 for 2 windows.
